memory_update.text: NVT is a high-relevance liquid-cooling and rack-power reference candidate for AI racks; despite large-cap size, its CDUs, manifolds, PDUs, NVIDIA/Siemens reference links, and disclosed liquid-cooling deployment base make it useful as a benchmark for smaller thermal/power candidates.

MOD has unusually direct data-center cooling evidence, including a USD 4B long-term Airedale capacity agreement through 2029, CDU products, immersion-cooling IP, and a new Data Centers reporting segment; verify customer concentration and margins.

POWL is a power-conditioning/switchgear second-order candidate for AI campuses; evidence supports exposure to data-center/AI-driven medium-voltage opportunities, but order lumpiness and backlog mix must be verified before upgrading confidence.

BELFB is a lower-attention component hypothesis for data-center power conversion via 48V power supplies and power shelves; needs hard evidence of AI-server design wins, hyperscaler qualification, and revenue mix.

For high-density AI racks, the chokepoint may split into two coupled subnodes: thermal loops/CDUs/manifolds/chillers and power path components/switchgear/48V conversion/PDUs. Qualification, uptime requirements, and reference architectures create potential switching costs.

Next Layer 1C should search for US-listed and ADR suppliers of pumps, valves, heat exchangers, sensors, specialty coolants, busbars, and certification/testing providers; current pass found stronger evidence in system/subsystem vendors than in pure component suppliers.

node: Thermal management and power-conditioning components for high-density AI racks
summary: Underfollowed Layer 1B expansion for AI-rack thermal and power-conditioning components. Reference context remains Vertiv/Eaton-style integrated infrastructure, but this pass prioritizes less obvious US-listed component and subsystem suppliers: liquid-cooling/CDU/rack power vendors, data-center cooling manufacturers, medium-voltage power-control suppliers, and server power-module suppliers. The strongest evidence in this pass is for nVent and Modine because both disclose AI/data-center liquid-cooling products, capacity expansion, and named ecosystem/reference-architecture links. Powell has direct power-distribution exposure but more project lumpiness and rising attention. Bel Fuse is the lower-attention component hypothesis: real data-center power-supply products exist, but AI-rack customer qualification and revenue mix still require verification. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
